zh.text: 更新通道与旧版 Electron 彻底分开：新旧两个启动器过去读的是同一个 releases/latest 清单，而老更新器只核 sha256、不认 zip —— 一旦最新版是 Tauri 产物，老用户点了「更新」就会被替换成打不开的文件（静默报废）。现在新框架固定读独立的 stable 通道，releases/latest 钉回旧 Electron；两边再也碰不到对方。注意：还在 0.2.0–0.2.5 的请手动换一次 0.2.6 的 exe（那些版本读的是旧地址，且「立即更新」在它们上面本来就装不上）

配套护栏，防止通道被改回去：打包后跑 node scripts/release-channel.mjs publish/verify 会把新清单推到 stable 通道并核对「releases/latest 不再下发我们签名的清单」，不通过就报错；scripts/audit-security.mjs 与一条 Rust 单测也盯着内置清单地址，谁把它改回 releases/latest，npm run check 与 CI 立刻红
账号管理里点「删除角色」不再连账号一起删掉：过去这条路径会按角色名反查到所属账号，然后把整个账号（连着里面另外两个角色）一起删除。现在走独立的删角色通道，只删你选中的那一个角色，账号与其余角色原样保留
角色的在线状态改为跟随客户端进程：之前判断依据是服务端端口，只要服务端开着就恒为在线，关掉游戏窗口后角色还停在「在线」。现在客户端一退出就立即回落为离线，账号卡片的在线统计随之更新
账号卡片底部的 ISK 合计改读实时钱包余额：之前读的是建号时写入的初始余额，与角色实际资产对不上（真机上同一个角色由 100,000 修正为 8,010,279,191）
军团与联盟徽标不再画成同一张图：服务端对没有专属徽标的军团和联盟会回同一张默认画，20px 下完全分不出来。现在有专属徽标就画徽标，没有就画军团 ticker / 联盟简称的短标识，形状与配色分开，并且直接读盘、不依赖主服务是否启动
账号卡片空槽位的按钮文案由「进入游戏建号」改为「进入游戏创建角色」，与槽位上「角色在游戏内创建」的说明一致
修掉「本地模组版本比市场还高、却提示有新版本」：可更新判定原先只比「两边版本不一样」，作者本机装着 1.0.5、市场还停在 1.0.4 时会挂出「有新版本 1.0.5 → 1.0.4」，点「更新」等于把模组降级。现在按数字段逐个比较，只有市场版本严格更高才算可更新，口径与外壳及现役版一致

en.text: Update channels are now fully separated from the legacy Electron build: both launchers used to read the same releases/latest manifest, while the old updater verifies sha256 only and cannot handle zips — as soon as the newest release was a Tauri artifact, a legacy user clicking update had their launcher replaced with a file it could not run (silent breakage). The new shell now reads its own dedicated stable channel and releases/latest is pinned back to the legacy Electron line, so the two never touch. Note: if you are on 0.2.0-0.2.5, install the 0.2.6 exe manually once — those builds read the old address, and their install step was already broken

Guardrails so the channels cannot drift back: after packaging, node scripts/release-channel.mjs publish/verify pushes the new manifest to the stable channel and asserts that releases/latest no longer serves a manifest we signed, failing loudly otherwise; scripts/audit-security.mjs and a Rust unit test also watch the built-in manifest URL, so any commit pointing it back at releases/latest turns npm run check and CI red immediately

Deleting a character in account management no longer takes the whole account with it: that path used to reverse-look-up the owning account from the character name and delete the entire account, including its other two characters. It now uses a dedicated delete-character channel that removes only the character you picked, leaving the account and its other characters untouched

A character's online state now follows the client process: it used to be derived from the server port, so it stayed online as long as the server ran, and a character still showed as online after you closed the game window. It now drops to offline the moment the client exits, and the account card's online count follows

The account card's ISK total now reads the live wallet balance: it used to read the initial balance written at character creation, which did not match the character's actual assets (on a real install one character went from 100,000 to 8,010,279,191)

Corporation and alliance logos no longer render as the same image: the server returns one shared default picture for corporations and alliances that have no dedicated logo, which is impossible to tell apart at 20px. A dedicated logo is drawn when one exists; otherwise a short badge shows the corporation ticker or alliance short name, with distinct shape and colour, read straight from disk so it no longer depends on the main server being up
The empty character slot button now reads “Create character in game” instead of “Create in game”, matching the “characters are created in game” note on the slot

Fixed “a local mod newer than the marketplace build still showed an update”: update detection compared only for inequality, so an author running 1.0.5 locally while the marketplace still listed 1.0.4 got “update available 1.0.5 → 1.0.4”, and clicking update downgraded the mod. Versions are now compared segment by segment and only a strictly newer marketplace build counts as an update, matching the shell and the legacy launcher
